title: Rapid synth: ICLR takeaways + deployable experiment ideas
content:
Quick context: went to ICLR workshops focused on inference + efficient LLM serving. Notes below are noisy — intended for quick handoff to the team and a few concrete experiments we can try on Redwood Dedicated clusters.

High-level themes I kept hearing:
- Distillation as a practical tool for latency-sensitive endpoints (not just research demos). Tradeoffs: cost of distillation step vs sustained cost savings.
- Prefix/latent caching + selective recompute: favoring smaller recomputes by caching intermediate KV states or distilled prompts.
- Mixing quantization and structured sparsity for low-bit friendly runtime kernels.
- Eval-first deployment: small gold prompt sets + streaming latency budgets to detect regressions post-quantization.

Paper / talk quick notes (my shorthand):
1) "Layerwise Distill+Cache for Low-Latency Dialogue" (poster, arXiv:2403.01234)
- Idea: distill high-attention behavior into a compact prefix that's cached per conversation cluster.
- Result: 2–3x latency drop on 16k-context setups, ~5–7% drop in some quality metrics but recoverable with short refocusing prompt.
- Ops notes: requires per-customer prefix store (~10–50KB per conversation cluster), eviction policy needed.
- Question: can we implement prefix store as an extra KVS layer in front of the runtime (fast NVMe) and rely on our batching engine to pull it?

2) "Quant-aware pruning for dense kernels" (oral)
- Weight-clipping + small structured prune step before 4-bit quant worked better than naive quant.
- Implication for serving: add a quick prune+recalibration pipeline in model onboarding to avoid quality cliffs.
- Implementation idea: add a model onboarding stage in the console where we run a calibrated prune->quant step and produce a "redwood-quant-profile" artifact with expected perf numbers.

3) "KV-shard consistency in heterogeneous clusters" (workshop talk)
- Split KV cache across devices but keep a consistent eviction frontier; uses a tiny central sequencer to avoid stale reads.
- Tradeoff: sequencer can be a hotspot; authors solved with a sharded ring buffer and eventual consistency for cold hits.
- Ops takeaway: for Dedicated we can experiment with a lightweight sequencer service and measure head-of-line latency impact.

4) "Small eval loops for large deployments" (lightning talk)
- Keep ~200 prompt set that captures customer-critical behaviors (hallucination, factuality, style). Run nightly regression checks after any model or quant rollout.
- We can adopt their approach and map each customer to an eval-set template. Integrate with Redwood Optimize alerts.

Concrete experiments to prioritize (ranked):
A) Prefix-store prototype on Dedicated (low effort) — target endpoints: chat agents with long convs
- Goal: reduce average token latency for >8k contexts by 30%
- Plan: implement a microservice that stores compressed distilled prefixes keyed by (customer_id, convo_cluster). Hook into routing: when request arrives, fetch prefix (fast path) and prepopulate KV cache.
- Success metric: mean tail latency (p95) improvement and tokens-per-dollar improvement.
- Risks: extra storage/IO; complexity in cache invalidation.

B) Onboarding prune+4bit pipeline (medium effort) — model onboarding flow
- Goal: produce quant profiles that avoid large quality drops; automate calibration tests on small evals.
- Plan: add a step in onboarding: 1) light structured prune (10–20%) 2) quantize to 4-bit 3) run templated eval with golden prompts 4) record profile artifact.
- Success metric: fewer rollbacks post-quantization, stable eval scores within threshold.

C) KV-shard sequencer on a test cluster (higher effort)
- Goal: measure sequencer overhead vs savings from sharded cache memory footprint.
- Plan: replicate the paper's ring buffer logic in a small service, run on a 4-node GPU cluster and measure H2 store/read latencies and correctness under churn.

D) Small nightly eval harness per-customer (low effort)
- Goal: detect regressions from model/quant rollouts quickly and automatically trigger canary rollback.
- Plan: build a tiny job generator that hits the deployed route with 200 golden prompts; compare metrics to baseline; integrate with console alerts.

Notes for implementation details / rough TODOs:
- Storage: use dedicated NVMe pool for prefix store, start with 100GB test dataset, keep LRU eviction. Need to estimate per-customer storage footprint assumptions. (Maya: can you add rough cost calc?)
- API: add optional header X-Redwood-Prefix-Key on requests so runtime can short-circuit KV prefill.
- Onboarding: add a UI toggle for "quant-calibrate" in the console model page; store the produced quant-profile artifact as metadata.
- Experiments: create repro jobs under repo 'repro-exps' + issue #142 (linked). Use the same tokenization + eval harness as Optimize team.

Open questions / risks:
- Security: storing per-conversation distilled prefixes may have PI leakage risks. Need privacy review and possible encryption-at-rest.
- Consistency: when prefix update happens mid-conversation, how to migrate safely? Consider versioned prefixes and runtime fallback to latest matching version.
- Economics: what's the break-even distillation cost vs tokens-saved? Need a quick model (Maya to run) for typical chat traffic shapes.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Sync with Maya to get rough cost/back-of-envelope for prefix storage (Maya + Levi) — target: 2024-07-25.
- Spin up tiny prototype of prefix-store microservice (Levi) and a synthetic workload to validate latency improvements.
- Draft onboarding quant pipeline PR template (Ibrahim + Levi) with test cases and minimal CLI.

Random conference bits worth saving:
- Workshop coffee chat: folks are comfortable doing distillation offline in private infra before pushing artifacts to hosted endpoints — aligns with our Dedicated + Private product.
- Several speakers emphasized 'eval-first' rollouts; this syncs with Redwood Optimize direction.

Hand-off notes for whoever picks this up: keep experiments small and measurable. Label test clusters clearly and try to avoid cross-contaminating Dedicated perf tests with production.

End of note. If this is useful I can flesh out an initial RFC (1–2 pages) and a quick cost model for prefix-store.
